examples.text: This microphone has very weak pickup.

glosses: Ellipsis of pickup truck.

examples.text: Franklin is beside himself, revving up the engine in the pickup.
I kept my window rolled up, eyes on the road, probably making the pickup man angrier with my silence.

glosses: Impromptu or ad hoc, especially of sports games and teams made up of randomly selected players.

examples.text: Rather than join a basketball league, James decided to play pickup.
At lunch we had a game of pickup hockey.
Trevor, like an Aussie outbacker, eats snacks and a pickup meal of bread, cantaloupe, olives, mangoes, and melon.

glosses: An instance of approaching someone and engaging in romantic flirtation and courting with the intent to pursue romance, a date, or a sexual encounter.

examples.text: Hey, thanks for the drink, but if this is a pickup, I'm not interested.

glosses: A person successfully approached in this manner for romance or sex.

examples.text: "Good Lord! I'm not stopping you from taking on all the pick-ups that come your way."
But what about the women who still go to bars — are they completely unaffected by these negative connotations? Hardly. No woman wants to think of herself as being an easy pick-up […]
Audball's latest pickup didn't seem to care where they were, or anything at all about alimony, palimony, or child support […]

glosses: In various games, the fielding or hitting of a ball just after it strikes the ground.

examples.text: The fourth seed was dominating her 20-year-old opponent with a series of stinging groundstrokes and athletic drive-volleys, striking again in game five when Paszek flicked a forehand pick-up into the tramlines.

glosses: An item that can be picked up by the player, conferring some benefit or effect; a power-up.

examples.text: Every step of the way you come across absolutely loads of aliens, pick-ups and new and weird obstacles to overcome.
Enter the graveyard if you want pick-ups, otherwise make a left under the archways to progress. When the pathway ends, you'll see two blocked-off tunnels and a switch between them.

glosses: The act of a challenging party or candidate winning an electoral district held by an incumbent party or candidate.

examples.text: The returns from the election show Apple Party candidate Jane Doe has made a pickup in the district of City West defeating Orange Party Incumbent Joe Smith

glosses: The act of answering a telephone.

examples.text: That's why the phone at the theater's on automatic pickup.

glosses: A relatively minor shot filmed or recorded after the fact to augment previous footage.
The act of collecting and taking away something or someone, usually in a vehicle.

examples.text: Owner Philip Schaffart said a precoronavirus Tuesday typically brought in $2,500 in revenue. This past Tuesday, he said, that amount dwindled to $300 as his place was open only for pickup and delivery.

glosses: A time during which passengers, such as school children, are picked up.

examples.text: These signs are friendly reminders for road users to slow down during drop-off and pick-up.

glosses: The rate at which a motor vehicle picks up speed.

examples.text: The Willys-Overland won't be the fastest car on the road or have the best pickup, but it will have a top speed of eighty miles per hour, and its makers are confident that no car in its class will excel it in economy of fuel and upkeep.
The more highly vaporized the mixture your carburetor delivers, the more power you get, which means higher speed, better pickup, smoother idling, more miles per gallon.

glosses: The condition of being picked up, or taken up; adoption by some entity.

examples.text: Newsweek gave it a big write-up, as did many trade journals, including, ^([sic]) Editor and Publisher. And our articles get pickup as far west as the Tombstone Epitaph in Arizona.
Back then CPI staff demonstrated a reflexivity common to public relations, reflected for instance in Lewis's acknowledgment of the fact that the novelty factor might lead to more pickup.

glosses: Appareil domestique appelé à l’origine phonographe et dont la dénomination a évolué en tourne-disque, électrophone et platine, et destiné à la lecture sonore des disques microsillons.

examples.text: Il m’emmena dans la salle voisine, la salle de bal traversée de guirlandes en papier, et me fit asseoir devant le pick-up.
Cependant le pick-up tournait, et peu à peu j’étais pris à mon tour dans le cercle des bras nus et des épaules fondantes des propos sans suite, des rires sans motifs.
Arrivé dans le coin par hasard, il n’y avait trouvé ni concurrence ni piano mécanique ni pick-up et s’y était fixé, vivant de son accordéon.
Puis ils mirent sur le pick-up un disque de Frankie Tornado, commis charcutier moins connu l’an passé sous le nom de Jules Poulailler.

Un doigt noir où tous les os marquaient sous la gaine de vieille peau se promenait sur sa paume ouverte et l’ongle glissait dans le creux des lignes à la façon d’une aiguille de pick-up qui va chercher les sons au fond du sillon.

Quand elle parvenait à s’isoler, Lucile écoutait sur le pick-up les chansons de Charles Trenet. Face au miroir, souriante et bien coiffée, elle chantait « Boum », « La Java du diable » ou « J’ai ta main », qu’elle connaissait toutes par cœur.

glosses: Véhicule utilitaire léger muni d’un plateau non recouvert à l’arrière.

examples.text: Des études sur simulateur (Rudin-Brown, 2004 ; Rudin-Brown et McCurdie, 2004 ; Lee, 1995), ainsi que des études expérimentales, laissent penser que les conducteurs de véhicules tout-terrain, de pick-up et de camionnettes évaluent leur vitesse avec moins de précision, parce qu'ils sont assis plus haut, au-dessus de la chaussée, que les conducteurs de voitures particulières.

La taille croissante des voitures a des conséquences concrètes dans nos rues: les gros SUV (Sport utility vehicle) et les pick-up à l’américaine ne tiennent pas dans les emplacements prévus et empiètent sur les trottoirs ou sur la route, commente Nicolas Raffin, porte-parole de Transports & Environnement.
Un pick-up rouge de marque Nissan a d’abord foncé dans sa voiture.
Une fraction de seconde avant que l'arrière du pick-up se soulève, comme un tapis-luge entraîné par une rafale, une immense toile d'araignée se déploya.
Il monte dans sa pick-up et s’en va à la recherche du camion qu’il attend.
(Parfois invariable) Un petit groupe d'une dizaine de pick-up, parmi lesquels je reconnus le Nissan Navara d'Aymeric, descendit lentement la bretelle d'accès à l'A13.
